findings-not-fitting-a-single-item.finding: Every registered project -- including the canonical winner itself (jsaa, already correct, nothing to fold) -- shows up under 'need a human to attribute' on any dry run that omits --map, because ADR-0099 made Default fully empty (no hardcoded canonicals at all, not even well-known ones). The scoreboard's 'need nothing (already correct or empty)' bucket only credits an id if the operator's own --map explicitly lists it as a canonical.
findings-not-fitting-a-single-item.evidence: first dry run (no --map): 'jsaa matches no known id (registered as jsaa) -- left alone for a human to attribute', 0 need-nothing out of 9. Second dry run (--map listing jsaa as a canonical): 1 need-nothing (jsaa), 6 need-attention.
findings-not-fitting-a-single-item.so-what: an operator with many registered, healthy projects will see ALL of them counted as 'need a human' on every map-less run, forever -- not a defect against ADR-0099's stated design (which explicitly rejected a persistent map), but a real UX rough edge worth a follow-up decision: either accept it as the documented cost of the one-shot --map model, or consider a way to let an operator's own canonicals persist across runs without reintroducing the rejected persistent-map alternative.
findings-not-fitting-a-single-item.recommendation: flag for the project owner; not a blocker for this release
